# Information security policy — sanctions clause to add

**Prepared:** 26 October 2026 · Kristian Boe Helweg Hansen, Compliance Manager
**Target document:** *Information security policy and objectives*, Cyberday version #7, generated
28.09.2026 (Cyberday group 8090). Filed for the audit as `C1 Information security policy and objectives.pdf`.
**Companion:** [`EMPLOYEE_SANCTIONS_AND_DISCIPLINARY_PROCEDURE.md`](EMPLOYEE_SANCTIONS_AND_DISCIPLINARY_PROCEDURE.md)
**Status:** Text ready to enter. **It cannot be applied from here** — the policy is generated by
Cyberday, not held as a file in this repository, so the clause has to be entered in Cyberday and the
policy re-exported.

---

## Why this is the one change that cannot be skipped

The Danish Data Processing Agreement signed with clients states, under *Organisatoriske
sikkerhedsforanstaltninger*, item 1:

> "Politikker og retningslinjer: Vi udvikler og implementerer klare sikkerhedspolitikker og
> retningslinjer, der definerer acceptable brugspraksisser, adgangsniveauer, dataklassifikationer,
> **ansvar og sanktioner i tilfælde af overtrædelser**."

The current policy contains no such definition. I searched the extractable text of version #7 for
*sanction*, *disciplinary*, *misconduct*, *violation*, *breach*, *non-compliance* and *consequence*,
and the only hits were "personal data breaches" in a list of documentation types. Responsibility and
sanctions are not addressed.

That is precisely the mismatch **ISAE 3000 control C.2** asks the auditor to look for: *"Management of
the data processor has checked that the information security policy does not conflict with data
processing agreements entered into."* The evidence requested is a documented mapping between the
policy and the contractual security requirements, including actions taken to resolve any gaps. A
mapping produced honestly today has to record this one as open.

The Staff Handbook is not a substitute. It is an employment document, it is not the policy named in
the DPA, and it has never been given to a client. The commitment is about the security policy.

---

## Where it goes

The policy's current structure is: *Policy overview* → *Leadership and commitment* → *Information
security objectives* → *Framework for setting information security objectives* → *Organisation's
framework* → *Objectives list* → *Overview of the ISMS* → *ISMS theme owners* → *ISMS themes*.

Add the clause as a **new section immediately after *Leadership and commitment*, before
*Information security objectives***. That position matters: it sits with the statements about what
management requires, rather than among the metrics, and it is above the fold for anyone who reads
only the first two pages — which, for an auditor sampling a policy, is most of them.

In Cyberday this is free text on the policy, not a task or a guideline. Enter it, publish a new
version, and re-export the PDF for the evidence folder so the filed `C1` document is the version
containing the clause.

---

## Clause text — English

> ### Responsibility and consequences of non-compliance
>
> Information security at Data & More depends on the people who work here, and this policy is
> binding on all of them. Every employee, contractor and student is responsible for following the
> security rules that apply to their work: the guidelines in this management system, the
> requirements in the Staff Handbook, and the instructions given by the controllers whose personal
> data we process. Managers are additionally responsible for ensuring that the people reporting to
> them know these rules and are able to follow them.
>
> Where the rules are not followed, Data & More responds in two separate ways, and they should not
> be confused with one another.
>
> The first is containment. Access, credentials or a device may be suspended immediately to limit
> the consequences of what has happened. This is a security measure, it is taken on the facts
> available, and it implies no finding of fault.
>
> The second is a sanction. Data & More applies the *Employee sanctions and disciplinary procedure*,
> which sets out six proportionate steps, from an informal conversation through a reminder, a
> written warning and a final written warning, to dismissal with notice and — for gross misconduct —
> summary dismissal. Which step applies depends on the seriousness of the breach, the harm it caused
> or risked, whether it was deliberate, whether it has happened before, and whether the person
> reported it themselves. Deliberate unauthorised access to personal data, removing data from the
> company, disabling a security control, falsifying a record, and concealing an incident are treated
> as gross misconduct. No sanction above an informal conversation is decided before the person has
> been told what is alleged and given a real opportunity to respond.
>
> Reporting is never punished. Nobody is sanctioned for reporting an incident in good faith,
> including one they caused themselves. Failing to report, or delaying a report, is itself a
> disciplinary matter.
>
> For contractors, students and suppliers there is no disciplinary relationship to apply. The
> response is instruction, suspension or withdrawal of access, and termination of the engagement or
> the agreement under its own terms. Access consequences are the same regardless of how a person is
> engaged.
>
> The *Employee sanctions and disciplinary procedure* is owned by the Compliance Manager, approved
> by the Partner, and reviewed annually.

## Clause text — Danish

Needed because the DPA is Danish and the commitment being answered is a Danish sentence. A client
or an auditor checking item 1 of *Organisatoriske sikkerhedsforanstaltninger* against an
English-only policy has to do the translation themselves.

> ### Ansvar og konsekvenser ved overtrædelse
>
> Informationssikkerhed i Data & More afhænger af de mennesker, der arbejder her, og denne politik
> er bindende for dem alle. Enhver medarbejder, konsulent og studerende er ansvarlig for at følge de
> sikkerhedsregler, der gælder for deres arbejde: retningslinjerne i dette ledelsessystem, kravene i
> personalehåndbogen og de instrukser, der gives af de dataansvarlige, hvis personoplysninger vi
> behandler. Ledere har derudover ansvaret for, at deres medarbejdere kender reglerne og er i stand
> til at følge dem.
>
> Når reglerne ikke følges, reagerer Data & More på to adskilte måder, som ikke må forveksles.
>
> Den første er inddæmning. Adgang, legitimationsoplysninger eller en enhed kan straks suspenderes
> for at begrænse konsekvenserne af det skete. Det er en sikkerhedsforanstaltning, den træffes på
> grundlag af de foreliggende oplysninger, og den indebærer ingen afgørelse om skyld.
>
> Den anden er en sanktion. Data & More anvender *Procedure for sanktioner over for medarbejdere*,
> som fastlægger seks proportionale trin: fra en uformel samtale over en påtale, en skriftlig
> advarsel og en sidste skriftlig advarsel til opsigelse og — ved grov misligholdelse — bortvisning.
> Hvilket trin der anvendes, afhænger af overtrædelsens alvor, den skade den forvoldte eller
> risikerede, om den var forsætlig, om den er sket før, og om den pågældende selv har anmeldt den.
> Forsætlig uberettiget adgang til personoplysninger, udtagning af data fra virksomheden, deaktivering
> af en sikkerhedsforanstaltning, forfalskning af dokumentation og fortielse af en hændelse behandles
> som grov misligholdelse. Ingen sanktion ud over en uformel samtale besluttes, før den pågældende er
> blevet gjort bekendt med det, der gøres gældende, og har haft en reel mulighed for at udtale sig.
>
> Anmeldelse straffes aldrig. Ingen sanktioneres for i god tro at anmelde en hændelse, heller ikke
> en, som vedkommende selv har forårsaget. Manglende eller forsinket anmeldelse er derimod i sig selv
> et disciplinært forhold.
>
> For konsulenter, studerende og leverandører findes der ikke et ansættelsesforhold at sanktionere.
> Reaktionen er instruks, suspension eller inddragelse af adgang samt ophør af samarbejdet eller
> aftalen efter dennes egne vilkår. Konsekvenserne for adgang er de samme uanset tilknytningsform.
>
> *Procedure for sanktioner over for medarbejdere* ejes af Compliance Manager, godkendes af
> partneren og revideres årligt.

## What this closes

| Control | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DPA, *Organisatoriske sikkerhedsforanstaltninger* item 1 | Commitment made, not met | Met, by the clause plus the procedure it names |
| ISAE 3000 C.2 | Policy/DPA mapping has an open row | Row closes, with the clause as the action taken |
| ISAE 3000 C.1 | Policy approved, but silent on consequences | Unchanged in form; re-approval needed for the new version |
| ISO 27001:2022 A.6.4 | *LOW / NOT COVERED* | Answered by the procedure, referenced from the policy |
| ISO 27001:2022 A.5.4 (Management responsibilities) | Policy states commitment but no enforcement | Enforcement stated |

## Before entering it

- [ ] **The sanctions procedure has to be approved first.** The clause names it. Entering the clause
      while the procedure is still a draft moves the dangling reference from the Handbook into the
      policy, which is worse, because the policy is the document clients are shown.
- [ ] **Decide the Danish title and use it consistently.** I have used *Procedure for sanktioner over
      for medarbejdere*. Whatever is chosen has to match the title on the procedure itself, the
      Handbook cross-references (Item 20 of the Handbook redline) and the Cyberday entry.
- [ ] **Confirm the six-step ladder and the Danish terms** with the employment-law review recorded as
      the first open point in the procedure. *Påtale*, *advarsel*, *opsigelse* and *bortvisning* carry
      specific meanings in Danish practice, and the policy should not state a ladder the review then
      changes.
- [ ] **Re-approval.** C.1 asks for management approval or review within the past year. A new policy
      version needs a dated approval, and the current one is dated 28.09.2026 — so this change should
      go in as part of a single reviewed version rather than as a silent edit.
- [ ] **Re-export and refile** the PDF as `C1 Information security policy and objectives.pdf`,
      replacing version #7 in the evidence folder. The filed evidence and the live policy must be the
      same version, or C.1 fails on the version rather than on the content.
- [ ] Check whether the clause should also appear in the Cyberday *Personnel security* theme summary,
      which currently lists tasks for contracts, training, guidelines and changes in employment
      relationships, but nothing about consequences.
